scenes.text: Turkey probably isn't the reason you feel sleepy after a Thanksgiving dinner.
The usual suspect is tryptophan, an amino acid found in turkey.
Your body uses it to make serotonin, which can be turned into melatonin, a sleep hormone.
But turkey has about as much tryptophan as chicken or beef.
And gram for gram, cheddar cheese actually has more.
Tryptophan also has to compete with other amino acids to get into your brain.
After a big protein meal, it's stuck in a crowd at the door.
Some scientists think the carbs on your plate may matter more than the turkey.
Potatoes, stuffing, bread and pie trigger insulin, which pulls many rival amino acids into your muscles.
That may let a little more tryptophan slip into the brain.
But the biggest culprit is simpler: studies show large meals of any kind make people drowsy.
Add a glass of wine, hours of cooking, and a house full of relatives.
So what really knocks you out after a holiday feast? Tell me below.

title: Turkey isn't why you're sleepy after Thanksgiving 🦃
caption: Turkey has about as much tryptophan as chicken or beef, and cheddar has more gram for gram. The post-feast slump is mostly the size of the meal, the carbs, and a long day.
